Sortable list – Components Reference – Live Wires

Sortable list

This optional enhancement moves an item into its requested position immediately. The visible order is provisional while your application decides whether and how to apply it.

This static reference includes a small local responder so the interaction can be tried. It updates each list as the application would, then confirms the matching request. It is an example only, not persistence or a server integration.

Use the handle and arrow keys to stage a position, Space to request it, and Escape to cancel. Dragging moves the row with the pointer; on release, it lands in the requested position while the application catches up. A rejection restores the previous position unless the application has already replaced the list markup. The move buttons request the previous or next position directly. In an application, point each form to its own reorder endpoint for a no-JavaScript fallback.

Use data-sortable-variant="cards" for separate bordered rows; omit it for simple dividers. data-sortable-density="compact" reduces text and spacing while keeping the controls' touch targets intact. Include a handle, move buttons, or both to choose the controls each list needs.

  1. Field notes — a link stays usable
  2. On paper — nested controls remain available
  3. An index

In a lined table

The same optional element can enhance rows inside a semantic table. The handle sits at the far left of each row. The table keeps its heading, row headers and horizontal rules, with no vertical borders.

Contract

The component emits a bubbling sortable-move-request event with { itemId, before, requestId } and immediately moves the row as provisional UI state. An empty before means append at the end. The application owns authorization, persistence, ordering and retry. Apply authoritative markup before calling list.resolveMove({ requestId, status, message? }) with accepted or rejected. Only a matching result clears pending state. A matching rejection restores the previous order only if the original item nodes are still in the provisional order; if the application has replaced the list markup, the component leaves those new nodes intact. The opaque request ID correlates this UI response; it is not an authorization or idempotency token. One move may be pending per list.

list.addEventListener('sortable-move-request', async (event) => {
  const { itemId, before, requestId } = event.detail;
  const result = await saveAuthorizedMove({ itemId, before });
  renderAuthoritativeList(result.items);
  list.resolveMove({ requestId, status: result.accepted ? 'accepted' : 'rejected' });
});

Use data-sortable-list, data-sortable-item, a unique data-item-id, data-sortable-handle, optional data-sortable-move="up|down", and data-sortable-status. Component styles use those hooks for the staged source, target, end cue, pending state and status. The reading-list example includes per-direction forms for a no-JavaScript fallback; the lined-table example uses buttons to demonstrate the client-side request flow. Applications can author fallback forms in table action cells too.

Load /dist/sortable-list.js and /dist/sortable-list.css only on pages that use the element. It is outside main.js. Removing an instance cancels staging and invalidates its outstanding request; reinsertion attaches one listener set and ignores old results. A consumer must render authoritative markup before calling resolveMove. The component never observes DOM changes as confirmation.
